thread:
anya: Heads-up — saw a customer hit repeated fallback hops during SSE warmup. Their client flips to a cheaper model variant, then back to primary; billing shows both tokens charged and latency spikes.

sam: ugh. any repro steps / logs?

anya: repro script attached inline:
```
curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"X-Fallback-Priority: cost,latency\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-3-13b
```

anya: pattern: client sends resume after ~8s, proxy routes to fallback pool, runtime accepts then immediately patient router routes back to primary once available -> double-count. console shows fastpath flag = true so UX hides the fallback trace.

mike: do we have an event emitted when fallback routing happens? I think current telemetry only logs final route.

lucy: right — console's fastpath view assumes single route. we hide intermediate hops to avoid noise, but that hides double-charge cases.

sam: can we add a short-lived span/event like `route_hop` with fields [from, to, reason] and a `billing_impact` tag? then console can aggregate if billing_impact>0 and show a warning.

anya: yes — and we should avoid emitting raw tokens on event (PII), just token_counts int. also need to include `edge_node` so we can correlate proxy vs runtime decisions.

mike: runtime change is small: emit RouteHop(event_id, from_route, to_route, reason, token_count_estimate). router change: emit when decision taken. both need same trace id.

lucy: console change: expose a checkbox in connection trace: \"show intermediate route hops\" off by default, but show an alert when billing_impact>0. also add a tooltip: \"Fallbacks are normal; this shows when two routes billed concurrently\"

anya: can we gate this behind a flag? we shouldn't flood prod with extra telemetry. propose a sample rate by tenant with `routing_hop_sampling` default 0.01 and a dev flag to force for single tenant.

sam: agree. add a dashboard card: `stream.route_hops` count, p50 time between hops, and `duplicate_token_charge` counter. alert if duplicate_token_charge > 5/min for a tenant.

mike: edge case: if client resumes quickly and we route to fallback then primary, we might still have inflight tokens counted by the billing pipeline even if runtime later dedupes. need to coordinate with billing to accept dedupe signals within 30s window. tagging billing_invalidation_id on RouteHop might help.

lucy: I'll prototype console UI and wire to a new Prometheus-like metric `redwood_stream_route_hops`. will add a small banner for affected tenants.

anya: runtime + router owners — can you add the RouteHop event to the next canary? label it `route_hop_v1` and add compatibility fallback so older consumers ignore it.

deploy-bot: canary rollout created: canary/route-hop-v1 -> eng-platform-us-west-2, 10% traffic.

sre-bot: FYI — monitoring rule `duplicate_token_charge` created in staging. default threshold 5/min.

sam: follow-ups: (1) confirm billing dedupe window with finance (2) confirm sampling defaults (3) console UX mock by EOW. anyone want to own item 1?

mike: I'll take billing dedupe sync.

anya: thanks — I'll open a short RFC with fields + example event schema and link to this thread.

lucy: ping me when RFC is up, will start mocks after. :+1:

anya: ok — filing RFC now, dropping logs & trace id samples in the ticket.

anya: end of thread — keeping minimal traces in console until we have sampling + alerting in place.
